statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-85091 is a heap buffer overflow in zlib's gz_write() in gzwrite.c: after an underlying write() fails, strm.next_in is left pointing at the caller's buffer, and a later gz* write call writes past a heap allocation. Upstream fixed it in commit df84af25 (https://github.com/madler/zlib/commit/df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148), first released in zlib 1.4, which clears strm.avail_in and resets strm.next_in to the state's input buffer when the write fails. Alpine backported that commit to zlib 1.3.2 in 1.3.2-r1 on 3.23-stable (https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/commit/b92621a82657b055485976b304462bddf9aa9183, https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-85091). Checked every published zlib and zlib-static package for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against the index checksum, by disassembling gz_write in libz.so and in gzwrite.o of libz.a: the instructions that clear strm.avail_in and point strm.next_in back at the input buffer after the failed write are present in 1.3.2-r1, 1.3.2-r2 and 1.4-r0 and absent in 1.3.1-r2 and 1.3.2-r0. 1.3.2-r1 is the first published build that carries the fix.

CVE-2026-85091 is a heap buffer overflow in zlib's gz_write() in gzwrite.c: after an underlying write() fails, strm.next_in is left pointing at the caller's buffer, and a later gz* write call writes past a heap allocation. Upstream fixed it in commit df84af25 (https://github.com/madler/zlib/commit/df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148), first released in zlib 1.4, which clears strm.avail_in and resets strm.next_in to the state's input buffer when the write fails. Debian fixed it in 1:1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1-1+deb13u1 with a backport of that commit to zlib 1.3.1 (DSA-6613-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/DSA-6613-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-85091). Two builds are published in the DHI Debian repository, and both carry the fix: the fixed version in this range, built from Debian's 1:1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1-1 source with a backport of the upstream fix that its shipped changelog records, and the rebuild of Debian's 1:1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1-1+deb13u1 source. Checked zlib1g and zlib1g-dev from both builds on amd64 and arm64, each verified against the index SHA256, by disassembling gz_write in libz.so.1.3.1 and in gzwrite.o of libz.a: after gz_comp() returns -1, both builds clear strm.avail_in and point strm.next_in back at the input buffer before returning, which is the change the fix makes. The same check finds no such instructions in an unfixed zlib 1.3.1 library (Alpine's zlib 1.3.1-r2). The fixed version is the lowest published build.
